code_semantics.trigger: last_tick exists AND (now < last_tick OR now-last_tick >0.08), using time.monotonic sampled after adapter gate lock acquisition.
code_semantics.effect: fail latches first fault, disarms; decision returns zero; control loop publishes zero then breaks; finally requests native stop and waits for feedback.
code_semantics.first_fault_retention: Gate.fail sets fault only when previously None; adapter result retains adapter_control_tick_invalid, not later native external_guard8.

observations: Fault zero command precedes supervisor stop_request_begin by~59ms; this is an execution-time adapter protection, not a normal-stop-induced fault.
Only one control_tick_invalid command is recorded and loop exits immediately; persistence of the latched reason does not demonstrate repeated timing violations or sustained loss of control.
Prior command reason was proposal_expired and output zero. Independent CAN reports zero throughout the1s before fault; no sustained nonzero velocity is evidenced around trigger.
Root stop-before and stop-after verification both confirmed; lifecycle reaches root_saved and observer exits normally.
Recorded CAN status entries around cleanup show state0/mode1/error0; native fault8 after adapter stop is separate protection state, not chassis error8.
unresolved: Previous actual last_tick and triggering interval are not retained: command journal deduplicates same signature to1s, so adjacent journal timestamps are not control-tick timestamps. Cannot recover precise gap, distinguish gap from monotonic regression solely from this record, or quantify multiple subthreshold delays.

Root actuator telemetry is subscribed but per-tick snapshots are not archived here. Snapshot last_control_tick is updated to current decision time, so even final state alone cannot recover previous interval.
No scheduler/lock-duration/CPU-trace evidence establishes cause; do not attribute to inference load, filesystem, CAN delay or driver malfunction.
